record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: For alpha >= 0, define the one-dimensional non-tangential maximal operator M_alpha by M_alpha f(x) = sup (2t)^{-1} integral_{y-t}^{y+t} |f(s)| ds over pairs (y,t) with t>0 and |x-y| <= alpha t. This interpolates between the centered operator M_0 and the uncentered operator M_1. For functions f: R -> R of bounded variation, does Var(M_alpha f) <= Var(f) hold for every 0 <= alpha < 1/3? More generally, what is the smallest alpha for which this sharp variation inequality holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a parameter $\alpha \geq 0$, define the one-dimensional non-tangential Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator $M_\alpha$ acting on locally integrable functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ by
$$M_\alpha f(x) \;=\; \sup_{\substack{t>0,\, y\in\mathbb{R} \\ |x-y|\leq \alpha t}} \frac{1}{2t}\int_{y-t}^{y+t} |f(s)|\,ds.$$
For $\alpha=0$ this is the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator, and for $\alpha=1$ it coincides with the uncentered maximal operator. For a function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, let
$$\mathrm{Var}(f) \;=\; \sup\sum_{i} |f(x_{i+1}) - f(x_i)|,$$
the supremum being over all finite increasing sequences $x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_N$ in $\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Determine whether the sharp variation inequality
$$\mathrm{Var}(M_\alpha f) \;\leq\; \mathrm{Var}(f)$$
holds for every $f$ of bounded variation and every $0 \leq \alpha < 1/3$.

(b) Determine the infimum of all $\alpha \geq 0$ for which the inequality $\mathrm{Var}(M_\alpha f) \leq \mathrm{Var}(f)$ holds for every function $f$ of bounded variation on $\mathbb{R}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The sharp variation bound $\mathrm{Var}(M_\alpha f)\leq \mathrm{Var}(f)$ is known for $\alpha\geq 1/3$ (Ramos, 2017; a more elementary proof appears in recent work by other authors who also extended the discrete case down to $\alpha=1/3$). The regime $0\leq \alpha<1/3$, including the centered case $\alpha=0$, remains unresolved; in particular the exact threshold $\alpha$ for which the sharp inequality holds is not known.

status_evidence.title: Sharp Total Variation Results for Maximal Functions — J. P. G. Ramos
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp total variation results for non-tangential maximal functions, proving the bound for parameter α ≥ 1/3.
status_evidence.claim: The sharp variation inequality is established for α ≥ 1/3.

status_evidence.title: Study of bounded variation on the H-L nontangential operator
status_evidence.snippet: For all α ∈ [1/3, +∞), Var(M^α f) ≤ Var(f); provides alternative proof in the continuous setting and extends to the discrete setting at the endpoint α=1/3.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art results cover α ≥ 1/3; α < 1/3 is not addressed.
